answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-resource staking. Each agent must lock a verifiable physical asset on chain—a weighed lot of ferrous scrap, a certified jade ingot, or a sealed timber shipment—and an oracle confirms the asset exists before admission. Every new identity demands its own distinct asset, so a sybil attacker minting thousands of accounts must source and register thousands of separate goods. Mass duplication shifts from free keypairs to real logistics and capital per fake node, pricing out cheap impersonation.
